options.label: Train on earlier rows, test on later ones
promises: Every test row is later than the latest train row.
options.definition:
import polars as pl


def temporal_split(
    data: pl.DataFrame,
    time_column: str,
    test_fraction: float = 0.20,
    group_column: str | None = None,
):
    """Split by time. Every train row is strictly earlier than every test row."""
    if data[time_column].null_count():
        raise ValueError(f"{time_column} has {data[time_column].null_count()} missing values")
    cutoff = data[time_column].quantile(1 - test_fraction, interpolation="lower")
    train = data.filter(pl.col(time_column) < cutoff)
    test = data.filter(pl.col(time_column) >= cutoff)
    # Train drops every item that is also in test, so no item is on both sides.
    if group_column is not None:
        train = train.filter(~pl.col(group_column).is_in(test[group_column].implode()))
    return train, test

plots.definition:
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import polars as pl


def rows_over_time(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame, time_column: str):
    figure = go.Figure()
    for name, side in (("train", train), ("test", test)):
        counts = side.group_by(time_column).len().sort(time_column)
        figure.add_bar(x=counts[time_column], y=counts["len"], name=name)
    figure.add_vline(x=test[time_column].min())
    return figure

import polars as pl
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit


def group_split(data: pl.DataFrame, group_column: str, test_fraction: float = 0.20, seed: int = 42):
    """Hold out complete entities so the same group never appears in train and test."""
    groups = data[group_column]
    if groups.null_count():
        raise ValueError(f"{group_column} has {groups.null_count()} missing values")
    if groups.n_unique() < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"{group_column} needs at least two distinct groups")
    splitter = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=test_fraction, random_state=seed)
    train_rows, test_rows = next(splitter.split(range(data.height), groups=groups.to_list()))
    return data[sorted(train_rows)], data[sorted(test_rows)]

import polars as pl
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split


def stratified_split(
    data: pl.DataFrame, stratify: str, test_fraction: float = 0.20, seed: int = 42
):
    """Shuffle rows into train and test, keeping each class's share on both sides."""
    if data[stratify].null_count():
        raise ValueError(f"{stratify} has {data[stratify].null_count()} missing values")
    train_rows, test_rows = train_test_split(
        list(range(data.height)),
        test_size=test_fraction,
        random_state=seed,
        stratify=data[stratify].to_list(),
    )
    return data[sorted(train_rows)], data[sorted(test_rows)]

plots.definition:
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import polars as pl


def class_shares(train: pl.DataFrame, test: pl.DataFrame, stratify: str) -> go.Figure:
    """Class shares in train and test"""
    figure = go.Figure()
    for name, side in (("train", train), ("test", test)):
        shares = side[stratify].value_counts(normalize=True).sort(stratify)
        figure.add_bar(x=shares[stratify], y=shares["proportion"], name=name)
    return figure
